children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were lower Tuesday morning, due to the mixed nature of the comparable oils.
Crude oil was a pinch higher, providing a little bit of spillover support to the vegetable oils. In Chicago, the soybeans were lower while the oil and meal notched small increases.
European rapeseed was pulling back but Malaysian palm oil was pushing upward.

Statistics Canada is set to issue its first crop production report Wednesday. Although record canola acres were planted this spring, given the varied conditions across the Prairies this growing season it's uncertain if there will be another record harvest or something less than the 21.81 million tonnes gleaned last year.
Last month Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada projected the canola harvest to be 21.6 million tonnes. The U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated the crop at 22.5 million tonnes.
Temperatures across the Prairies Tuesday are to be in the mid-teens Celsius, with rain expected for southern Alberta.
Canola crush margins increased with the November positions between C$272.90 to 283.70 per tonne above the futures.
The Canadian dollar eased back Tuesday morning with the loonie slipping to 71.81 U.S. cents, compared with Monday's close of 71.90.
About 14,800 contracts had been traded by 9:40 a.m. ET and prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne were:
